{"T0.help":"The aim here is to divide featureless galaxies from all the rest. *Please consider only the galaxy in the center of the image in your answer.* If the central galaxy is interacting with another galaxy, you will be able to tell us about that in a later question. For this question, ignore nearby galaxies and foreground stars that are in front of the central galaxy.  If you can see any interesting features at all in the central galaxy, or if you think it is an edge-on disk, click "Features or Disk".

Occasionally you might see something that isn't a galaxy at all -- the long streak of a satellite, for example, or an image swamped by light from a bright star. If this obscures the galaxy, click "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom". In Galaxy Zoo: Cosmic Dawn, you may occasionally find galaxies that are too small or too large in the image for you to classify, such as a galaxy that extends outside the image, in which case you should click "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom". This does **not** apply to reasonably-sized galaxies that just appear blurry. **Only tick the "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom" box if the galaxy is unclassifiable due to either a star/artifact or the galaxy being far too large or small within the image.**

**Smooth**
The galaxy gradually fades in all directions from the center. There may be a small bright symmetric core.

**Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom**

**When should I choose "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom"?**

Choose "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom" if there is no central galaxy to classify, the central galaxy is far too large or small in the image (e.g. extending outside of the image, or too small to even see) or if the artifact is so bad that you can't ignore it and classify the galaxy with reasonable confidence.

The telescopes taking our data were designed to look at faint galaxies, which means that bright, compact objects like stars sometimes look a bit strange:

![star_artifact_102010568_NEG830174551609614594_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/c05060a1-2f56-4497-a9ba-5f979e7d4d2e.jpeg =150x) ![UDS_25098_WFC3_bright_star.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/c48e8704-88bc-46a2-9fab-304a6fb56429.jpeg) ![SDSS bright stars](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237672024630102787.jpg) ![GDS_22517_WFC3_medium_star.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/dc4e6556-3b4f-4d12-941f-fd464b909b4c.jpeg) ![UDS_25098_WFC3_bright_star.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/c48e8704-88bc-46a2-9fab-304a6fb56429.jpeg) ![SDSS diffraction spikes](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237668332566675568.jpg) ![COS_25147_TWO_bright_stars.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/f5695a0c-b251-4d74-98a0-e17e33284a77.jpeg) ![sloan-0_a-2_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-0_a-2_0.jpg =150x) ![sloan-0_a-2_1.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-0_a-2_1.jpg =150x)

The telescope takes deep images that mean we can see many more distant galaxies in the same patch of sky. But this many galaxies can sometimes confuse the software used to focus on each individual galaxy to create the images you see, resulting in images that are too zoomed-in or zoomed-out:

![star_or_artifact_102010923_NEG817334814606598825_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/4f21e83d-e983-49c9-b2c5-0bdcc6151439.jpeg =200x) ![bad_zoom_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/604a0393-472c-4fc8-8e60-a0b8505ce624.png =200x) ![bad_zoom_3.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/945196a3-ce3b-474a-b5f7-f57ffb502c6e.png =200x) ![bad_zoom_7.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/26d50325-5816-444f-b8a5-b2365c873a31.png =200x)

In ground-based images, things like satellites can pass overhead while the camera shutter is open. Or, a diffraction spike from a nearby star can also make a line across the image (note one of these has a classifiable galaxy):

![artifact_102010923_NEG818284504604771630_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/3c5ae59e-1cb7-4b16-86f3-4aee2bcc7c0f.jpeg =150x) ![satellite trails](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237679253598765338.jpg) ![satellite trail 2](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237671762629820436.jpg)

Sometimes weird things happen when you get to the edge of the camera chip:

![COS_1_CANDELS_chip_artifact.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/5f020cbd-6286-4b96-b6b2-efd46ccad5cf.jpeg) ![COS_8_CANDELS_chip_artifact.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/cf5ff7b7-ec09-4183-bb79-3fd9c26e9cea.jpeg)

And sometimes something just... goes a bit weird:

![olives... in...](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237664620098552177.jpg) ![...spaaaace...](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237656232029127081.jpg) ![oops, the telescope moved](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237654896296264385.jpg) ![bright star nearby](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237678437017583659.jpg) ![oops, bad data](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237668585434316837.jpg)

Occasionally you might see something that *is* astronomical, but isn't a galaxy, like a nebula or star-forming cloud from our own galaxy:

![1237667725903790995](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/4c0ac87c-7bd3-40ff-86e4-75c1a2c19a1e.jpeg =150x) ![1237667726977663041](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/9d50d618-135c-4480-b441-f33277e1b8ed.jpeg =150x) ![1237667726977663100](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/534e8966-7f00-4636-985e-800bb9bb7474.jpeg =150x)

These are often very pretty, but they're not galaxies, so please mark them as "Star, Artifact, or Bad Zoom" -- but feel free to discuss them on Talk!","T1.help":"Look at the overall shape and decide how round it is. Remember to always concentrate on the galaxy in the centre and ignore any other galaxies.

**Completely round**
![sloan-7_a-0_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-7_a-0_0.jpg =200x) ![AHZ2000jnr](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20066328.jpg =200x) ![AHZ40002wy](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/90020800.jpg =200x)

**Inbetween**
![sloan-7_a-1_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-7_a-1_0.jpg =200x) ![20015991](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20015991.jpg =200x) ![AHZ2001627](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20142106.jpg =200x)

**Cigar-shaped**
![AHZ20009dq](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20030058.jpg =200x) ![AHZ2000z88](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20118746.jpg =200x) ![AHZ40002wd](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/90019630.jpg =200x)

*Note*: "cigar-shaped" smooth galaxies can look a lot like edge-on disk galaxies. Edge-on disks are often thinner than cigar-shaped ellipticals. They also tend to come to more of a point at either end, so people use the "pointy ends" test: if it has them, it's more likely an edge-on disk than a cigar-shaped elliptical.

These are *edge-on disks* (which we'd call "featured or disk" in the previous question):
![1237680507724300460.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/5dea91c0-3b65-487d-b10b-f474f0c9ce17.jpeg =200x) ![AHZ2000j54](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20064554.jpg =200x) ![AHZ2001rx8](http://zoo-hst.s3.amazonaws.com/20154144.jpg =200x)","T2.help":"Disk galaxies tend to be very flat, like a pancake or frisbee, and sometimes they are tilted so that we see them from the side. When that's the case, we can't see the other details of their structure. These galaxies should be labelled as edge-on so that we know what we *can't* know about what else might be in the disk. 

Some examples of edge-on and not-edge-on disks (to see many more, check the *Field Guide*):

**Yes - Edge On Disk**
The galaxy looks too tilted to see whether its disk has structures (such as spiral arms).
*Note: edge-on disks may still have bulges (example below).*
![sloan-1_a-0_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-1_a-0_0.jpg =200x)![This is edge-on *enough* that we can't see the details.](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/1821036b-79ca-442e-96e1-d98e4749a51e.jpeg =200x)
![Edge-on disk with a bulge](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/e4dea284-096d-4f9d-a453-a5a03d51a38f.jpeg =200x)![You can see there's dust, but you can't see whether the disk has a spiral or a bar](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/671b37a3-c297-4554-adaa-e8e83d1c9b11.jpeg =200x) ![H20_HSC_lz_2216_cutout.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/6032d39c-fcdb-426b-9dce-1d1ea83a8ce0.png =200x)

**No - Something Else**
The galaxy is face-on enough to see whether there are other structures in the disk, or it is not a disk at all (e.g. an irregular galaxy).
![Face-on disk with spiral structure](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/4382faba-2b1b-4219-8951-3b126ffd71fa.jpeg =200x)![Tilted, but you can still see the details](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/27b0e971-33d0-4a82-aaae-da87de853077.jpeg =200x)

If the galaxy bulges outwards in the center, select Rounded or Boxy depending on the shape of the bulge.

**Rounded**
The galaxy has a central bulge which is smoothly curving.

![rounded_0_1.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/be57a61d-6082-491b-a1f1-b0083681f6f0.png =200x) ![rounded_0_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/0be6de56-40b8-46c1-a611-9c4c39da7ff9.png =200x) ![decals-7_a-0_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-0_0.jpg =200x) ![decals-7_a-0_1.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-0_1.jpg =200x) ![decals-7_a-0_2.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-0_2.jpg =200x) ![decals-7_a-0_3.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-0_3.jpg =200x)

**Boxy**
The galaxy has a bulge which is shaped like a box or like an 'X'. 

![box_bulge_0_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/16907b8f-9d33-4e5d-b5b6-77a3662b360b.png =200x) ![box_bulge_0_1.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/9b90c46a-962f-4b5f-9dea-3183d3e3d50c.png =200x) ![x_bulge_0_4.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/991cdd7c-b439-41cd-9f51-181a7be831f2.png =200x) ![x_bulge_0_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/c40d849d-7332-4c03-ada4-30bc1a0450ee.png =200x) ![x_bulge_1_4.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/3ff64705-f70a-48cc-8bd3-03f2858f4a96.png =200x) ![x_bulge_1_3.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/project_attached_image/da5cf08b-60d1-49d8-9a29-76c7a9e103ef.png =200x) ![decals-7_a-1_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-1_0.jpg =200x) ![sloan-8_a-0_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-8_a-0_0.jpg =200x) ![sloan-8_a-1_0.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/sloan-8_a-1_0.jpg =200x) ![decals-7_a-1_2.jpg](https://static.zooniverse.org/www.galaxyzoo.org/images/examples/decals-7_a-1_2.jpg =200x)

There are 3 most commonly-seen types of objects that aren't actually galaxies.

### Stars

![star_artifact_102010568_NEG830174551609614594_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/c05060a1-2f56-4497-a9ba-5f979e7d4d2e.jpeg =200x) ![star_3.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/50e1a7fc-39ac-4722-917d-c6d7e1bf2633.png =200x) ![star_4.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/288bb95a-77f2-4413-9ee6-1d1042df0272.png =200x) ![star_5.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/8790d574-e3a7-42ed-83d1-d7dff3425822.png =200x) ![star_8.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/7acc3630-67bb-4b5f-ba04-cc5f8b9fb855.png =200x) ![star_9.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/f718dc76-4a62-4aaf-8f62-ef9fb6c0c183.png =200x)

A star is a foreground object from our own galaxy, not a distant galaxy. Stars are "unresolved" by telescopes, which means they usually just look like very compact points of light. Bright stars will often also show other things like diffraction spikes and saturation trails, which are due to the telescope configuration and instrumentation.

### Non-star Artifacts

![satellite trails](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237679253598765338.jpg =200x) ![artifact_1.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/3447754d-abf9-400a-a1cd-d3bf2a35d5b1.png =200x) ![oops, bad data](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237668585434316837.jpg =200x) ![oops, the telescope moved](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237654896296264385.jpg =200x) ![...spaaaace...](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237656232029127081.jpg =200x) ![bright star nearby](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237678437017583659.jpg =200x)

These can be instrumentation related, such as image ghosts from a nearby bright star, or they can be things in space that aren't stars or galaxies, such as cosmic rays, asteroids or satellite trails. Some of these are astrophysically useful in their own right, so we want to identify them for possible study in the future, and we also want to learn how to filter them better from Galaxy Zoo.

Occasionally you might see something that *is* astronomical, but isn't a galaxy, like a nebula or star-forming cloud from our own galaxy:

![1237667725903790995](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/4c0ac87c-7bd3-40ff-86e4-75c1a2c19a1e.jpeg =200x) ![1237667726977663041](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/9d50d618-135c-4480-b441-f33277e1b8ed.jpeg =200x) ![1237667726977663100](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/production/subject_location/534e8966-7f00-4636-985e-800bb9bb7474.jpeg =200x)

These are often very pretty, but they're not galaxies, so please mark them as "Non-star artifact" -- but feel free to discuss them on Talk!

### Bad Image Zoom

![bad_zoom_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/604a0393-472c-4fc8-8e60-a0b8505ce624.png =200x) ![bad_zoom_3.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/945196a3-ce3b-474a-b5f7-f57ffb502c6e.png =200x) ![bad_zoom_7.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/26d50325-5816-444f-b8a5-b2365c873a31.png =200x) ![DECaLS_76773096_bad_zoom.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/b4be2ee4-4296-439a-bf49-fd4e3e75f60b.png =200x) ![DECaLS_75130561_bad_zoom_and_star_spike.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/873f79bb-df3f-4ae5-a774-2d08aea7c128.png =200x) ![DECaLS_76773667_bad_zoom.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/91702650-1092-4bf0-b5fb-87d6491875a7.png =200x)

We try to show you galaxies zoomed in at the right level so that you can see the details of the galaxy and some of the sky context around it, but sometimes the algorithms get it badly wrong. Telling us when you see these helps us get it right more often in the future. Please note that this option does **not** apply to reasonably-sized galaxies that just appear blurry.","T15.help":"There are multiple types of artifacts that can be present in astronomical images. These can be instrumentation related, such as image ghosts from a nearby bright star, or they can be things in space that aren't stars or galaxies, such as cosmic rays, asteroids or satellite trails. Most of these are found and filtered out automatically prior to Galaxy Zoo, but some can go undetected, so identifying these can help improve this automated filtering. Additionally, some of these are astrophysically useful in their own right, so we want to identify them for possible study in the future, and we also want to learn how to filter them better from Galaxy Zoo.

**Saturation Feature (Bleed Trail)**

The bright light of nearby stars can saturate the telescope's detector and artificially cause adjacent pixels to brighten (called "bleeding" of the light). These can obscure the light of distant galaxies (note that the galaxies here are all still classifiable):

![DECaLS_76768430_star_spike.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/f0fe45e4-1687-49c4-8bfb-fa0c221fb283.png =150x) ![DECaLS_76772622_star_spike.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/8679bb91-1b35-4459-a328-63109d969c02.png =150x) ![DECaLS_76772285_star_spike.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/b4d7f115-1c4e-4028-a6f0-d774b9344761.png =150x) ![DECaLS_76775065_star_spike.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/197d29e1-c176-442a-a676-96d6ad50d4ee.png =150x)

**Diffraction Spike**

As point sources, the light of nearby stars can also become diffracted by parts of the telescope, seen in images as radial lines emanating from the star (like spokes of a wheel):

![DECaLS_spikes_2.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/437eef23-4a32-4b0f-a9e9-1f2676c5333c.png =150x) ![DECaLS_spikes_3.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/f422cd24-8617-448a-b0b9-0a07df1266aa.png =150x) ![DECaLS_spikes_4.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/d5bd8dc0-fcdc-4df1-80e5-75e5d14c4faf.png =150x) ![DECaLS_spikes_5.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/80e66fe1-64e5-4cc8-808e-17087c1aa824.png =150x)

**Satellite Trail**

Things like satellites can pass overhead while the camera shutter is open (note one of these has a classifiable galaxy):

![satellite trails](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237679253598765338.jpg) ![satellite trail 2](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237671762629820436.jpg)

**Cosmic Ray**

High energy particles can impact the Earth's atmosphere and occasionally produce secondary particles that enter a telescope's detector, appearing as small streaks or 'worms' in images (note that the galaxies here are all still classifiable):

![DECaLS_20532371_cosmic_rays.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/dd4535ab-932e-48f8-8feb-28a37430e3cd.png =150x) ![DECaLS_20927464_cosmic_rays.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/632adfaa-b0e5-4cd0-812a-a8d91f8c3940.png =150x) ![DECaLS_28487746_cosmic_rays.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/be6de621-b89e-4e79-ae50-c8370d0bcd8a.png =150x) ![DECaLS_27364588_cosmic_rays.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/59410cf4-4b34-4e0f-b695-c657d2209aaa.png =150x)

**Scattered Light**

Images can sometimes be dominated by large swathes of light that block out anything behind it. While occasionally due to light scattered in the atmosphere that has not been completely accounted for, it is often instead due to the presence of a nearby bright star just out of frame:

![bright star nearby](https://s3.amazonaws.com/www.galaxyzoo.org/subjects/thumbnail/1237678437017583659.jpg) ![artifact_1.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/3447754d-abf9-400a-a1cd-d3bf2a35d5b1.png =150x) ![DECaLS_21660953_artifact.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/32b72229-2dd5-456a-8549-d4e2cb9832ee.png =150x)  ![H20_HSC_lz_593514_cutout.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/579dbcc7-8a30-40d1-b053-30e52ba96c02.png =150x)

**Ghost**

Ghosts are a specific kind of scattered light. They show up due to nearby bright objects that cause light to reflect in a particular way, showing rounded shapes. 

![artifact_not_a_galaxy_102010923_NEG820565677602605763_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/dcb19934-36bb-4d57-a54a-0a7b46835f12.jpeg =150x) ![artifact_102010569_NEG843415509607963067.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/57093104-9d09-41b3-9bc3-6e3bf1e039ba.jpeg =150x) ![DECaLS_59710037_artifact.png](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/5fb4961e-5e3e-4f01-810c-a33384eb4e41.png =150x) ![artifact_102010569_NEG841523044610324214_anno_500.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/f190e7b7-bb7e-4541-bf67-6853006f7c14.jpeg =150x)

This encompasses any artifacts or objects that do not fit into the above categories, or any that you are particularly unsure about.

For example, sometimes weird things happen when you get to the edge of the camera chip:

![COS_1_CANDELS_chip_artifact.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/5f020cbd-6286-4b96-b6b2-efd46ccad5cf.jpeg) ![COS_8_CANDELS_chip_artifact.jpg](https://panoptes-uploads.zooniverse.org/project_attached_image/cf5ff7b7-ec09-4183-bb79-3fd9c26e9cea.jpeg)
